questions.q: What is a project? *

o.t: A routine operation performed by an organization
A temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result
A sequence of ongoing operational tasks
A set of continuous activities with no clear end date

questions.e: According to PMI, a project is a temporary endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result. It has a definite beginning and end.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a project charter? *

o.t: To authorize the project and give the project manager authority
To define detailed project requirements
To create the work breakdown structure (WBS)
To track project performance

questions.e: A project charter formally authorizes the existence of a project and provides the project manager with the authority to use organizational resources for project activities.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)? *

o.t: To define the project's schedule
To organize and break down project work into manageable components
To list all project risks
To create a network diagram

questions.e: The WBS is a hierarchical decomposition of the total scope of work to be carried out by the project team. It helps manage work efficiently.

questions.q: What does the term "stakeholder" refer to in project management? *

o.t: A person or group that provides funding for the project
An external party with no direct involvement in the project
An individual, group, or organization affected by the project or who can influence its outcome
Only the customer who will receive the project deliverables

questions.e: A stakeholder is any individual, group, or organization that may be affected by or can influence the project. This includes sponsors, customers, team members, and regulators.

questions.q: What is the Triple Constraint in project management? *

o.t: Cost, Schedule, Scope
Quality, Risk, Budget
Communication, Stakeholders, Performance
Time, Procurement, Cost

questions.e: The Triple Constraint, also known as the Iron Triangle, consists of Cost, Schedule, and Scope. Changes in one constraint typically impact the other two.

questions.q: What is a project milestone? *

o.t: A significant event in the project schedule, typically with no duration
A critical activity in the project plan
The completion of the project deliverables
A final deadline for project completion

questions.e: A milestone is a significant point in a project, often marking the completion of a major phase or deliverable, and it has zero duration.

questions.q: What is the difference between a project and an operation? *

o.t: A project is temporary, while an operation is ongoing and repetitive
A project has no clear objective, while an operation does
A project involves daily tasks, while operations do not
Projects and operations are the same in nature

questions.e: Projects are temporary endeavors with a specific start and end date, whereas operations involve ongoing, repetitive work necessary for business continuity.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of risk management in a project? *

o.t: To avoid all possible risks
To identify, analyze, and develop responses to potential project risks
To assign blame for project failures
To increase the number of contingency reserves

questions.e: Risk management aims to identify potential threats and opportunities, analyze their impact, and create strategies to mitigate negative effects or enhance positive ones.

questions.q: What is the Critical Path in project management? *

o.t: The shortest path through the project network diagram
The sequence of project activities that determines the minimum project duration
A list of high-priority project tasks
The total float available in a project

questions.e: The Critical Path is the longest sequence of activities that must be completed on time for the project to be finished on schedule. Delays in critical path tasks directly impact the project's end date.

questions.q: What is Earned Value Management (EVM)? *

o.t: A method for tracking the amount of money spent in a project
A performance measurement technique that integrates cost, scope, and schedule
A technique for forecasting the financial profitability of a project
A scheduling tool used to track progress

questions.e: Earned Value Management (EVM) is a technique that integrates cost, scope, and schedule to assess project performance and forecast future trends.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a project scope statement? *

o.t: To outline project risks and response plans
To formally authorize the project
To describe the project objectives, deliverables, and boundaries
To create a schedule for project tasks

questions.e: The Project Scope Statement clearly defines the project’s objectives, deliverables, assumptions, constraints, and boundaries to ensure all stakeholders have a shared understanding of what the project includes and excludes.

questions.q: What does the term "progressive elaboration" mean in project management? *

o.t: Adding new requirements to the project scope over time
Developing project details in an iterative manner as more information becomes available
Completing the most important project tasks first
Repeating project phases until perfection is achieved

questions.e: Progressive elaboration means continuously refining and detailing a project plan as new information is discovered, improving accuracy over time.

questions.q: What is a project baseline? *

o.t: The originally approved version of the project plan, including scope, schedule, and cost
A list of project risks and their impacts
The collection of stakeholder requirements
The planned project end date

questions.e: A project baseline is the approved version of a project’s scope, schedule, and cost, against which performance is measured.

questions.q: What is a key function of the Project Management Office (PMO)? *

o.t: To execute all projects within the organization
To establish governance, standards, and best practices for managing projects
To directly fund all project activities
To replace project managers in large organizations

questions.e: The PMO (Project Management Office) is responsible for setting standards, best practices, governance, and oversight for projects within an organization.

questions.q: What is a stakeholder register? *

o.t: A formal document listing all project team members
A document identifying project stakeholders, their interests, influence, and engagement strategies
A document tracking project risks
A communication plan for reporting project progress

questions.e: The Stakeholder Register lists all stakeholders, along with their level of influence, expectations, and strategies for engagement.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a risk register? *

o.t: To store all project documentation
To track identified risks, their analysis, and planned responses
To define the project scope
To list team members and their roles

questions.e: The Risk Register is used to document identified risks, their probability and impact, response strategies, and mitigation plans.

questions.q: What does "lead" mean in project scheduling? *

o.t: The amount of time an activity can be delayed without delaying the project
The amount of time a successor activity can start before the predecessor finishes
The critical activity in a project schedule
The float time of an activity

questions.e: Lead time refers to the amount of time a successor activity can start before its predecessor activity finishes.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an issue log? *

o.t: To track project problems and their resolutions
To document project risks
To maintain meeting notes
To store change requests

questions.e: The Issue Log helps track problems or concerns that arise during the project, including their status and resolution.

questions.q: What is the role of a sponsor in a project? *

o.t: To manage day-to-day project tasks
To provide funding and executive support for the project
To directly supervise the project team
To create the project schedule

questions.e: A project sponsor is typically a high-level executive who provides funding, support, and guidance for the project.

questions.q: What is the difference between qualitative and quantitative risk analysis? *

o.t: Qualitative analysis prioritizes risks based on impact and likelihood, while quantitative analysis assigns numerical values to risks
Qualitative analysis uses mathematical models, while quantitative analysis is based on subjective judgment
Qualitative analysis is done in the execution phase, while quantitative analysis is done in the initiation phase
There is no difference; both methods are used interchangeably

questions.e: Qualitative risk analysis ranks risks based on impact and probability, while quantitative risk analysis assigns numerical values to estimate the effect on project objectives.

questions.q: What is a Change Control Board (CCB)? *

o.t: A group responsible for reviewing and approving project changes
The project sponsor and customer team
A tool for tracking project risks
A document listing all approved project changes

questions.e: The Change Control Board (CCB) is a committee that reviews, evaluates, and approves or rejects project change requests.

questions.q: What is project procurement management? *

o.t: The process of acquiring goods, services, or results from external sources
The process of assigning work to team members
A method for managing project communication
A budgeting technique

questions.e: Procurement management deals with contracting, purchasing, and acquiring resources or services from external vendors.

questions.q: What is the main goal of a lessons learned register? *

o.t: To document insights and experiences from a project for future use
To track project schedule deviations
To maintain a log of project meetings
To list project risks

questions.e: The Lessons Learned Register captures key takeaways, successes, and mistakes from the project to help future projects improve.

questions.q: What is meant by "gold plating" in project management? *

o.t: Adding extra features beyond what was originally agreed upon
A risk management technique
A method of estimating project costs
The process of obtaining project approval

questions.e: Gold plating refers to delivering extra features that were not part of the agreed scope, which can lead to unnecessary costs and risks.

questions.q: What is a Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM)? *

o.t: A tool that defines roles and responsibilities for project tasks
A schedule management tool
A document that tracks project risks
A procurement tracking system

questions.e: A Responsibility Assignment Matrix (RAM), such as a RACI chart, defines who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for project tasks.
